synoptic.summary: A negatively tilted trough brings a cold front down the I-15 corridor around 05:00–08:00 Saturday, with widespread rain overnight, a wind shift to flow from 330°–350° and gusts to 25 kt at the airports, and post-frontal showers tapering through Saturday afternoon. A short-lived ridge follows Sunday and Monday: dry, cold start Sunday with light flow from 150°–180°; by Monday the flow from 190°–225° strengthens aloft (20 kt at ~5,300 ft and ~40 kt at ~9,300 ft above the POM landings) ahead of the next, colder storm on Tuesday.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: This cold front will stretch the entire length of the I-15 corridor from southwestern Utah up through the Idaho border between 5-8 am. This front will move through quickly with drier air moving in behind it across southwestern Utah.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure has fallen from 1016.0 mb (01:54Z Fri) to 1003.3 mb (00:54Z Sat) — a deep fall ahead of the front. Expect a sharp rise and gusty post-frontal flow from ~330° on Saturday, then a brief ridge Sunday–Monday before the next trough on Tuesday.

observations.summary: Friday evening (00:15–00:50Z, current at run time): pre-frontal flow from 165°–210° at 5–12 kt across both valleys, light rain at Provo. Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no observations. These are evening readings ~13 h before the Saturday morning slot and will be overturned by the cold front — they say little about Saturday morning; they match the forecast's pre-frontal flow from ~150°–170° up to the frontal passage.
